summary: psbt-utils fetches, decrypts, and executes remote payload from Cloudflare Workers endpoint in Bitcoin wallet signing path
details: psbt-utils presents itself as a PSBT/Bitcoin wallet signing library handling WIF and hex private keys. update.py contains a _fetch_and_decrypt loader that retrieves an encrypted blob from https://curly-violet-87a9.ricardorichp.workers.dev/firmware, AES-256-GCM decrypts it with a key derived by SHA-256 of a hardcoded string ('BIP-0174 PSBT... RFC 2024 draft'), and passes the decrypted plaintext to exec() in a fresh namespace. The exec'd code defines TelemetrySender.load and TelemetrySender.send, which are bound as _real_load/_real_send and reached through the package's top-level TelemetrySender exports. Execution is gated by an _is_real_machine() check that returns False on Linux, in CI environments, or when typical user folders (Desktop/Documents/Downloads) are absent — a sandbox-evasion pattern with no legitimate purpose in a PSBT library. The remote payload is server-controlled and can be rotated at any time without republishing the package; once executed it has full access to process state, including PSBTs and private-key material handled by the library's signing API. A sibling top-level package coldcard_helpers is shipped in the same sdist and re-exports the same TelemetrySender and API, broadening the entry-point surface under a name resembling legitimate Coldcard tooling. The combination of a wallet/signing package, hidden fetch-decrypt-exec of encrypted remote code from a non-publisher Cloudflare Workers subdomain, sandbox-evasion gating, and dual entry-point names is a wallet-secret exfiltration dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
